review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

3:1.sourceText: Τούτου χάριν ἐγὼ Παῦλος ὁ δέσμιος τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν τῶν ἐθνῶν—
3:1.targetText: For this cause, I Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you the nations,

3:2.sourceText: εἴ γε ἠκούσατε τὴν οἰκονομίαν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ τῆς δοθείσης μοι εἰς ὑμᾶς,
3:2.targetText: if, indeed, you heard of the dispensation of the grace of God that was given to me in regard to you,

groups.note: Greek heard directly governs the dispensation object; English hear of expresses that same information/experience complement without an independently printed Greek of preposition.

3:3.sourceText: ὅτι κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν ἐγνωρίσθη μοι τὸ μυστήριον, καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ,
3:3.targetText: that by revelation He made known to me the secret, according as I wrote before in few [words]—

groups.note: N1904 ἐγνωρίσθη is passive was made known; LSV made known follows TR active ἐγνώρισεν. The knowing/revealing predicate is shared, while the added active English subject He remains separately noted.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness voice/agent difference: LSV He made known follows TR active ἐγνώρισεν; N1904 ἐγνωρίσθη is passive was made known, with secret as its grammatical subject and no expressed He agent.
Bracketed English words explains the in-few/briefly expression; N1904 has ἐν ὀλίγῳ without a words noun.

3:4.sourceText: πρὸς ὃ δύνασθε ἀναγινώσκοντες νοῆσαι τὴν σύνεσίν μου ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
3:4.targetText: in regard to which you are able, reading [it], to understand my knowledge in the secret of the Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English reading object is supplied from the preceding writing; Greek has no accusative object pronoun with reading.

3:5.sourceText: ὃ ἑτέραις γενεαῖς οὐκ ἐγνωρίσθη τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὡς νῦν ἀπεκαλύφθη τοῖς ἁγίοις ἀποστόλοις αὐτοῦ καὶ προφήταις ἐν Πνεύματι,
3:5.targetText: which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men, as it was now revealed to His holy apostles and prophets in the Spirit—

groups.note: The dative other-generations phrase is rendered temporally as in other generations, without a separately printed Greek in preposition.

3:6.sourceText: εἶναι τὰ ἔθνη συνκληρονόμα καὶ σύνσωμα καὶ συνμέτοχα τῆς ἐπαγγελίας ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου,
3:6.targetText: that the nations are fellow-heirs, and of the same body, and partakers of His promise in the Christ, through the good news,

groups.note: The infinitive εἶναι supplies the content of the revealed secret; LSV converts it to a that-clause, that the nations are. Both English that and are belong to the same infinitival-to-finite constituent.
The compound adjective σύνσωμα means fellow-members of a body; LSV expresses it as of the same body. This is the whole co-body-membership phrase, not separate Greek of/same/body words.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness title difference: N1904 adds Jesus after Christ; LSV/TR has no Jesus at this occurrence.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness possessive difference: LSV His promise follows additional TR αὐτοῦ; N1904 has no possessive with promise.

3:7.sourceText: οὗ ἐγενήθην διάκονος κατὰ τὴν δωρεὰν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεοῦ τῆς δοθείσης μοι κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ.
3:7.targetText: of which I became a servant, according to the gift of the grace of God that was given to me, according to the working of His power;

3:8.sourceText: ἐμοὶ τῷ ἐλαχιστοτέρῳ πάντων ἁγίων ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις αὕτη, τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαι τὸ ἀνεξιχνίαστον πλοῦτος τοῦ Χριστοῦ,
3:8.targetText: to me—the less than the least of all the holy ones—was given this grace, among the nations to proclaim good news—the untraceable riches of the Christ,

groups.note: The unusual comparative built on least, ἐλαχιστοτέρῳ, is rendered less than the least, retaining its intensified humility rather than inventing several Greek comparison words.
The dative recipient phrase τοῖς ἔθνεσιν accompanies proclaim-good-news; LSV describes this recipient sphere as among the nations. The relation belongs to the whole case-marked noun phrase.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:9.sourceText: καὶ φωτίσαι τίς ἡ οἰκονομία τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ ἀποκεκρυμμένου ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων ἐν τῷ Θεῷ τῷ τὰ πάντα κτίσαντι,
3:9.targetText: and to cause all to see what [is] the fellowship of the secret that has been hid from the ages in God, who created all things by Jesus Christ,

groups.note: The causative illumination verb φωτίσαι is rendered to cause ... to see. The separate English all is a source-witness addition, not the Greek all-things object of created borrowed across predicates.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness noun difference: N1904 ἡ οἰκονομία is the dispensation/administration, whereas LSV the fellowship follows TR ἡ κοινωνία. The unlike nominal heads are not conflated.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness object difference: LSV all after cause follows additional TR πάντας, absent at this first occurrence in N1904. The actual later τὰ πάντα remains linked to created all things.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
Source-witness noun difference: LSV fellowship follows TR κοινωνία rather than N1904 οἰκονομία, dispensation/administration.
Source-witness addition: LSV by Jesus Christ follows additional TR διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ; N1904 ends with created all things.

3:10.sourceText: ἵνα γνωρισθῇ νῦν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς ἐξουσίαις ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις διὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἡ πολυποίκιλος σοφία τοῦ Θεοῦ,
3:10.targetText: that there might be made known now to the principalities and the authorities in the heavenly [places], through the Assembly, the manifold wisdom of God,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English noun completes the substantival heavenly phrase; no separate places noun is printed in Greek.

3:11.targetText: according to a purpose of the ages, which He made in Christ Jesus our Lord,

3:12.sourceText: ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν παρρησίαν καὶ προσαγωγὴν ἐν πεποιθήσει διὰ τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ.
3:12.targetText: in whom we have the freedom and the access in confidence through the faith of Him,

3:13.sourceText: διὸ αἰτοῦμαι μὴ ἐνκακεῖν ἐν ταῖς θλίψεσίν μου ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν δόξα ὑμῶν.
3:13.targetText: for this reason, I ask [you] not to faint in my tribulations for you, which is your glory.

groups.note: ἐνκακεῖν denotes losing heart/becoming discouraged, rendered faint figuratively; no literal unconsciousness is claimed.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English object of ask is supplied; Greek αἰτοῦμαι has no explicit accusative you here.

3:14.sourceText: Τούτου χάριν κάμπτω τὰ γόνατά μου πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα,
3:14.targetText: For this cause I bow my knees to the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness title addition: LSV follows the longer TR τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ after Father; pinned N1904 ends with the Father.

3:15.sourceText: ἐξ οὗ πᾶσα πατριὰ ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς ὀνομάζεται,
3:15.targetText: of whom the whole family in the heavens and on earth is named,

review.note: N1904 πᾶσα πατριά is anarthrous and admits every family; LSV the whole family gives a collective whole-family interpretation. The actual universal quantifier and family noun are retained without claiming that all/every/whole readings settle the interpretive question.

3:16.sourceText: ἵνα δῷ ὑμῖν κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ δυνάμει κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον,
3:16.targetText: that He may give to you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened through His Spirit with might, in regard to the inner man,

groups.note: The instrumental dative δυνάμει is rendered with might; with expresses the actual case relation of the whole power/might noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:17.sourceText: κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστὸν διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν, ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἐρριζωμένοι καὶ τεθεμελιωμένοι,
3:17.targetText: that the Christ may dwell through the faith in your hearts, having been rooted and founded in love,

groups.note: The infinitive κατοικῆσαι describes the granted Christ-dwelling outcome; LSV converts it into the finite that ... may dwell clause. Both English markers belong to that clausal recast, not separate Greek that/may words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

3:18.sourceText: ἵνα ἐξισχύσητε καταλαβέσθαι σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἁγίοις τί τὸ πλάτος καὶ μῆκος καὶ ὕψος καὶ βάθος,
3:18.targetText: that you may be in strength to comprehend, with all the holy ones, what [is] the breadth, and length, and depth, and height,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

review.note: N1904 lists breadth, length, height, depth, while LSV lists breadth, length, depth, height. Each actual dimension noun stays linked to its own English counterpart; the leading conjunctions follow their dimensions through the reordered English list.

3:19.sourceText: γνῶναί τε τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν τῆς γνώσεως ἀγάπην τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἵνα πληρωθῆτε εἰς πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ Θεοῦ.
3:19.targetText: to know also the love of the Christ that is exceeding the knowledge, that you may be filled—to all the fullness of God;

3:20.sourceText: Τῷ δὲ δυναμένῳ ὑπὲρ πάντα ποιῆσαι ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ ὧν αἰτούμεθα ἢ νοοῦμεν κατὰ τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἐνεργουμένην ἐν ἡμῖν,
3:20.targetText: and to Him who is able to do exceedingly [and] abundantly above all things that we ask or think, according to the power that is working in us,

groups.note: The intensified compound adverb ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ is rendered exceedingly [and] abundantly. Both English adverbs belong to that one actual source word; the bracketed connective is separately supplied.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English conjunction separates the two adverbial senses of the compound ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ; Greek has this one intensified adverb, not a coordinating καί.
